patch_description:
This implementation replaces the item-by-item Python greedy packer with a vectorized folded block-packing strategy. Experts are sorted by load, split into equal-capacity blocks, and each block is assigned so its heaviest entries go to the currently lightest packs. This preserves exact per-device capacity while substantially reducing Python-loop overhead.

Replica allocation uses a batched marginal water-filling formulation. Instead of repeatedly computing a maximum for every additional replica, it selects the largest replica-benefit marginals in one `topk` operation when the candidate matrix is reasonably sized. This produces the same minimax-style replica allocation principle while improving parallelism. A memory-safe iterative fallback is retained for unusually large configurations.

The hierarchy remains topology-aware: groups are first distributed across nodes, replicas are created only within node-local expert pools, and physical replicas are then folded onto GPUs within each node.
